panel.name: plus_presets
panel.panel.string: Applying the graphics settings. The viewer stands still for a few seconds (up to about 20 seconds the first time a combination is used, while its shaders are prepared).

The Charis graphics presets are now part of the quality slider (Preferences > Graphics, the photo tools' Quality tab: seven levels from Low to Ultra). The preset you used is now the "[LEVEL]" level; your draw distance and avatar limits are as they were.
The Charis graphics presets are now part of the quality slider (Preferences > Graphics, the photo tools' Quality tab: seven levels from Low to Ultra). Your graphics settings are as they were.

The Charis graphics presets are now the quality slider (Preferences > Graphics, the photo tools' Quality tab: seven levels from Low to Ultra). The preset for comparing with the official viewer you were using is now Preferences > Charis > Development > Comparison. The draw distance and the avatar limits are as they were.

The Mid-High quality level is new: distant avatars are drawn more simply (flat pictures beyond 25 m, still grey figures beyond 45 m) and loading objects materialize with a band of light. Press Undo to go back to how it was (only the settings changed are put back). You can also change them later: "Draw avatars as pictures beyond" and "Make jelly dolls beyond" (0: off) in Preferences > Graphics, and "Materialize objects as their textures arrive" in the advanced settings. To compare with the official viewer, use Preferences > Charis > Development > Comparison.

The Mid-High quality level is new: distant avatars are drawn more simply (flat pictures beyond 25 m) and loading objects materialize with a band of light. Press Undo to go back to how it was (only the settings changed are put back). You can also change them later: "Draw avatars as pictures beyond" (0: off) in Preferences > Graphics, and "Materialize objects as their textures arrive" in the advanced settings. To compare with the official viewer, use Preferences > Charis > Development > Comparison.

The comparison settings now also draw textures still loading grey, as the official viewer does (no wireframe). To go back to how it was, press Undo; the comparison is then no longer shown as in use (press Comparison again to have it back). Choosing a quality level again brings the wireframe back too.
The OIT and anisotropic filtering values were also set to what the official viewer uses on this PC's GPU.
